relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a boy with Blau syndrome carrying a NOD2 variant: "heterozygous nucleotide substitution from C to T at position c.2798+158C>T in intron 8".
method_note: Read and transcribed by hand; no tables in the paper. One in-scope person (label 'patient', rule 5). Parents and two siblings were only examined clinically ('Examination of available family members including parents and two siblings did not reveal uveitis, skin, or joint abnormalities'); they were neither genetically tested nor affected, so they get no rows (uncertain scope). The transcript is recorded as printed ('NM_0022162.1'), which looks malformed; not corrected. Variant type 'other' reflects the authors' description as an intronic nucleotide substitution; they do not call it splice. No pathogenicity class stated beyond 'a mutation in NOD2 gene' in the abstract, recorded as not reported. Ages: the boy is '10-year-old' at referral ('2 years ago'), with later follow-up over at least 1 year; no age at onset (cataract surgery '6 years earlier', age at cataract onset not stated), last evaluation or diagnosis is stated, so all left not reported. 'No previous history of uveitis' refers to before referral and is not recorded as an exclusion because uveitis developed later. Normal intraocular pressure recorded as excluded raised IOP but the checklist item 'glaucoma or raised intraocular pressure' is left not reported (glaucoma not addressed; IOP only at first presentation). Normal uveitis workup (CBC, renal and liver function tests, chest CT) recorded as one excluded row in the paper's words; it is not used to exclude renal failure, interstitial lung disease or other checklist items. Retinal vascular sheathing/leakage is not counted as checklist vasculitis. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (no statement). No contradictions found.

span: lens aspiration and intraocular lens implantation 6 years earlier in both eyes
Pars plana vitrectomy with 360° retinectomy and silicone oil injection was performed in the left eye
3 doses of 1 g intravenous (IV) methylprednisolone daily were administered followed by oral prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day with weekly tapering and oral methotrexate 15 mg weekly
Subcutaneous adalimumab injections at 40 mg dosage every other week were initiated
The patient was maintained on 5 mg oral steroids, 15 mg oral methotrexate weekly, and every other week adalimumab
